usage: na3am is the neutral yes of Modern Standard Arabic and la is the neutral no, used in every register from news broadcasts to textbooks. MSA also has a separate yes, bala, that is only used to contradict a negative question. In everyday speech each dialect swaps na3am for its own word, such as aywa or eh.

variants.label: formal yes
variants.note: A literary yes, found in writing and formal speech.

variants.label: yes, after a negative question
variants.note: Use to answer "isn't it...?" with a yes.

variants.label: emphatic no
variants.note: A strong no, common in writing and speeches.

variants.label: of course
variants.note: A warmer yes when the answer is obvious.

examples.english: Yes, I speak a little Arabic.
No, thank you, I do not want coffee.

examples.arabic: أَلَيْسَ هَذَا كِتَابَكَ؟ بَلَى، هُوَ كِتَابِي.
examples.transliteration: alaysa hadha kitabaka? bala, huwa kitabi.
examples.english: Isn't this your book? Yes, it is my book.
